projects.name: LumaCV: AI Resume Intelligence
projects.description:
**Problem:** Resume tailoring is a manual, error-prone process that often fails ATS screening due to poor keyword alignment, inconsistent formatting, and AI rewrites that quietly invent facts. 
**Solution:** Built a free, open-source resume-building platform that extracts resumes client-side, tailors bullets against a target JD across a multi-provider BYOK AI layer, fact-checks every AI edit against the source before it reaches the client, scores the result with a deterministic (non-AI) ATS algorithm, and typesets it natively with Typst. 
**Impact:** Cut resume tailoring from ~30 minutes to under 60 seconds, with a server-side anti-hallucination validator as the product's core trust guarantee and vector PDFs across 52 ATS-safe templates.
projects.summary: Open-source AI resume platform with anti-hallucination fact validation, deterministic ATS scoring, and native Typst PDF typesetting.

detail.overview: LumaCV is a free, open-source resume-building SaaS (Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Supabase, Typst). A user pastes or uploads an existing resume, text is extracted entirely client-side (the file never reaches the server), an LLM structures it into typed resume data, the user optionally tailors bullets against a pasted job description, a server-side fact validator strips or reverts anything the AI invented, a deterministic algorithm scores the result against the JD, and the Typst typesetting engine compiles it to a vector PDF. The product's stated design center: "the AI can rephrase, it cannot invent."
stackHighlights: Next.js 14 App Router with a server/client component split for per-page SEO metadata
Multi-provider LLM orchestration (Gemini, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, GitHub Models system fallback; Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq BYOK)
Supabase Auth, Postgres + RLS, no ORM (direct PostgREST)
Upstash Redis rate limiting, bypassed for BYOK callers
Native Typst CLI compilation via child_process, bundled as a platform binary

architecture.title: Resume Builder Client
architecture.detail: Multi-step wizard (Upload/Paste + JD → Edit Details → AI Tailoring → Preview + Score) with persistent client state and zero-upload client-side PDF/DOCX text extraction.

architecture.title: AI Orchestration + Fact Validation
architecture.detail: BYOK across 4 providers plus 5 system fallback providers for resilience; every tailored response is run through a server-side validator that locks employer names, dates, and credentials, and reverts any bullet containing a fabricated metric before it reaches the client.

architecture.title: PDF Compilation
architecture.detail: child_process.spawn against a bundled Typst binary—typesetting itself completes in 20-45ms, producing 40-120KB vector PDFs with clean ATS-parseable text, versus rasterized HTML-to-PDF output.

decisions.title: Native Typst over LaTeX or HTML-to-PDF
decisions.context: HTML-to-PDF risks rasterized text and floating divs that ATS parsers misread; LaTeX is precise but heavyweight and slow to compile
decisions.decision: Compile via the native Typst CLI (not WASM)—pure vector glyphs, guaranteed top-down reading order, 20-45ms typesetting, at the cost of bundling a platform-specific binary and Node-only (non-Edge) compilation

decisions.title: BYOK plus system fallback, not a single provider
decisions.context: A single AI provider outage blocks every user, and free users need a usable default without configuring anything
decisions.decision: 4 BYOK providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq) for users who bring their own key and bypass the shared rate limit, backed by 5 system fallback providers for everyone else

decisions.title: Deterministic ATS scoring, not another AI call
decisions.context: An LLM-scored ATS match is unverifiable and non-reproducible, undermining the product's explainability claim
decisions.decision: Edge-rendered, sub-50ms keyword-match formula with dynamic weight renormalization across only the JD categories actually present, so an empty 'preferred skills' list can't cap a well-matched resume at 80%

decisions.title: Server-side fact validation as a non-negotiable invariant
decisions.context: LLMs can invent metrics, titles, or employers that a candidate never had, and prompt-level instructions alone aren't a reliable guardrail
decisions.decision: Every tailored resume is fact-checked server-side before reaching the client; any bullet containing a metric not traceable to the source resume reverts to the original text entirely, not just the invented number

pipeline.detail: Auto-deploy from GitHub; postinstall re-downloads/caches the native Typst binary each build
Sliding-window rate limiting on AI endpoints, skipped entirely for BYOK callers
maxDuration: 60 for AI/tailor routes on Node serverless; Edge runtime for the deterministic ATS score and stats endpoints

incidents.title: Export success reported on a failed compile
incidents.resolution: Traced through 4 consecutive point releases (2.15.1→2.16.3): removed a fake-PDF fallback string, rebuilt Word export as real OOXML, swept ~60 unguarded .trim() crashes with a safeTrim() helper, and fixed a Zod validation error being handed to the toast layer as a raw object
incidents.lesson: A failed export must fail loudly—never synthesize a fallback file to paper over a real error, and re-examine a 'fixed' bug rather than assuming the first patch found the root cause

incidents.title: IDOR on resume and application writes
incidents.resolution: Added explicit user_id ownership checks before upsert on any client-supplied resource id
incidents.lesson: Never trust a client-supplied id for ownership—verify server-side on every write, even for authenticated users

incidents.title: Vercel build silently missing the Typst binary in production
incidents.resolution: Bundled bin/ and typst/ into every API route via outputFileTracingIncludes, since local dev reads the filesystem directly and gives zero signal that production bundling is broken
incidents.lesson: A dev-only code path that happens to work by accident hides real production bundling regressions—verify against the actual deploy artifact, not just local behavior

projects.name: Claude Superpack
projects.description:
**Problem:** Skill packs for Claude Code fail in one of two directions—stay small and carry no real engineering judgment, or load so much always-on context that every turn pays for domain knowledge used once a month, with no mechanism to verify a claimed fix actually works.
**Solution:** Rebuilt from a 33-skill always-loaded pack into a 9-skill risk-tiered engineering OS that sizes every task on two independent axes (scope and risk), pulls in 15 domain references only when a task needs them, and runs 4 deterministic Node scripts instead of asking the model to eyeball diffs, secrets, and build logs.
**Impact:** Cut always-on context 73% (2,753 -> 742 tokens, cross-checked against Claude Code's own estimator) while adding capabilities v4 never had—a debugging skill, an evidence gate before any completion claim, and a high-precision credential scanner—then shipped it as a public npm package with GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing.
projects.summary: Risk-tiered engineering OS for Claude Code: 9 skills, 15 on-demand domain references, and deterministic verification scripts, published to npm with 73% less always-on context than its own v4.
metrics: Published to npm with GitHub Actions OIDC provenance

detail.overview: claude-superpack is an engineering operating system for Claude Code: nine always-on skills classify every request on two independent axes—scope (how much work) and risk (what happens if it's wrong)—then route into fifteen domain references and four deterministic scripts that load only when the task actually needs them. One rule overrides everything else: no completion claim without evidence produced after the change. Published to npm with GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing so every version is verifiably built from the repository.
stackHighlights: Two-axis task sizing: Scope (S0-S3) x Risk (R0-R3) sets planning depth and gate count independently
9 skills: 4 content-activated (debugging, securing, shipping, requirements-grilling) + 5 phase-activated, reached from a core gate table

15 domain references (frontend, backend, data, ai-llm, cloud, devops, sre, security, performance, testing, architecture, quality, docs, parallel, routing), each structured Decide first / Build right / Failure modes / Evidence
4 zero-dependency Node scripts: recon.mjs, gates.mjs, diffstat.mjs, secrets.mjs
Published as @sahilbnsll/claude-superpack via GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing with signed provenance attestation
Three-tier benchmark suite (structure, routing vocabulary, paired live evaluation) gates every release via npm run bench

architecture.title: Core Routing & Sizing
architecture.detail: Classifies every request on scope and risk, then routes to phase-activated skills via an explicit gate table—the only way those skills can be reached, since nobody types "I would like a blast-radius check now."

architecture.title: Domain References
architecture.detail: 92KB of engineering depth that costs zero always-on tokens and loads only when the router selects it, versus being baked into an always-loaded skill description.

architecture.title: Deterministic Scripts
architecture.detail: Replaces model guesswork with real tool output—secrets.mjs found 4 real credentials across 1,094 changed lines in 40ms with zero false positives; gates.mjs turned 15,247 bytes of build output into a 288-byte digest that preserved the evidence line.

beforeAfter.after: ~742 tokens across 9 skills (v5), cross-checked against Claude Code's own estimator

beforeAfter.label: Completion claims
beforeAfter.before: Model asserted a fix worked based on its own read of the diff
beforeAfter.after: Evidence gate blocks any completion claim without tool output produced after the change

beforeAfter.label: Codebase awareness
beforeAfter.before: Persistent JSON knowledge graph under ~/.claude/graphs/, which went stale silently
beforeAfter.after: Blast radius computed fresh from the diff and grep every time—slower per call, never confidently wrong

beforeAfter.label: Cross-session memory
beforeAfter.before: Five skills wrote to ~/.claude/memory/, duplicating dedicated memory plugins
beforeAfter.after: Removed entirely; defers to claude-mem or Claude Code's native memory, keeps in-task state in durable plan files

detail.architectureMermaid:
flowchart TD
  U[User request] --> C[superpack: classify scope x risk]
  C -->|content-activated| CA[debugging-systematically / securing-changes / shipping-safely / grilling-requirements]
  C -->|gate table| PA[codebase-recon -> planning-changes -> verifying-evidence -> reviewing-before-done]
  PA --> DR[15 domain references, loaded on demand]
  PA --> SC[recon.mjs / gates.mjs / diffstat.mjs / secrets.mjs]
  SC --> EV[Evidence gate]
  EV --> DONE[Completion claim]

decisions.title: Two independent axes instead of one A/B/C/D tier
decisions.context: v4's single complexity tier conflated "big" with "dangerous"—a 1,000-line refactor of a test helper and a one-line IAM policy change got identical treatment
decisions.decision: Split into Scope (S0-S3, sets planning depth) and Risk (R0-R3, sets gate count), so a trivial edit gets one tool call and a production/IaC change doesn't execute until blast radius is stated out loud and confirmed

decisions.title: Delete the persistent memory system and codebase graph
decisions.context: v4's ~/.claude/memory/ and ~/.claude/graphs/ cost context every session, duplicated dedicated memory plugins, and depended on the model reliably self-reporting its own state—a paired evaluation found that compliance happened once in eighty trials despite the instruction reaching the model every time
decisions.decision: Removed both. Blast radius is now computed fresh from the diff and grep on every task; cross-session recall defers explicitly to claude-mem or Claude Code's native memory instead of reimplementing it

decisions.title: npm publishing via GitHub Actions OIDC, not a stored token
decisions.context: A long-lived npm token sitting in CI is a standing credential that can leak or go stale
decisions.decision: Trusted publishing authenticates through GitHub Actions' OIDC identity—no npm token exists to leak—and every version carries a signed provenance attestation tying it to the exact workflow run that built it

pipeline.detail: Three-tier benchmark (148 structure checks, routing vocabulary coverage, paired live-evaluation harness) must pass before any release; prepublishOnly re-runs it with --no-write so published tarballs stay reproducible from their commit
Three independent jobs (verify, npmjs, github-packages), each skipping a version that already exists on that registry, so re-running a release is always safe
Every published version carries a signed attestation tying it to the workflow run that built it, verifiable via npm view @sahilbnsll/claude-superpack dist.attestations
No install scripts and no global install required—current npm blocks postinstall scripts by default, so a global install previously downloaded the package and silently skipped installing the skills

incidents.title: Global install silently skipped installing the skills
incidents.resolution: Removed postinstall/preuninstall entirely as a breaking change (v5.0.2); install is now an explicit `npx ... install` step that exits non-zero on failure instead of a lifecycle script that swallowed errors
incidents.lesson: A package that writes into the user's home directory merely by being downloaded is a supply-chain smell regardless of whether it currently works—npm blocking install scripts by default was the signal this needed fixing, not the cause of the bug

incidents.title: Every skill description loaded twice
incidents.resolution: v4 installed each skill both at ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ and again as a plugin-shaped copy underneath, roughly doubling always-on token cost to ~5,600 tokens/turn; the installer now installs one copy, deletes any leftover duplicate, and `claude-superpack doctor` detects the condition going forward
incidents.lesson: An installer needs an install manifest, not an assumption that its own previous version installed cleanly

incidents.title: Published tarballs weren't reproducible from their commit
incidents.resolution: prepublishOnly ran the benchmark suite, which rewrote a results file with a fresh timestamp on every publish, so the packed tarball never matched the commit and left the working tree dirty; prepublishOnly now runs with --no-write
incidents.lesson: A pre-publish hook that mutates the working tree undermines the exact guarantee—build reproducibility—that provenance attestation exists to provide

projects.name: Naukri Automation Bot
projects.description:
**Problem:** Keeping a Naukri profile active requires daily manual resume uploads, taking time and easily forgotten.
**Solution:** Developed an automated Python bot that runs 24/7 on Render's free tier, performing headless browser automation to update the resume on a scheduled basis.
**Impact:** Zero-touch profile refreshing ensures continuous recruiter visibility with 100% automation and bypasses OTPs via session persistence.
projects.summary: Headless Python automation on Render that uploads resumes to Naukri.com daily to maximize recruiter visibility.
metrics: Zero cold starts on Render free tier

incidents.resolution: Configured memory-saving Chrome flags and added exponential backoff on transient failures to respect Render's 512MB RAM cap

incidents.title: Job uploads failing due to unexpected OTP prompts
incidents.resolution: Engineered session extraction via export_cookies.py and added base64 cookie injection to bypass authentication flows smoothly
incidents.lesson: Repeated automated logins inevitably face bot detection—session persistence is mandatory for reliable long-term headless tasks

projects.name: LinkedIn Content Automation Pipeline
projects.description:
**Problem:** LinkedIn content creation is time-intensive, repetitive, and often lacks real-time relevance, reducing posting consistency. 
**Solution:** Built an AI-driven n8n automation pipeline with live research, LLM-based generation, and Discord-triggered workflows with Supabase state management. 
**Impact:** Automated end-to-end ideation to publishing, reducing effort from hours to seconds and enabling consistent, high-quality output.
projects.summary: AI-assisted LinkedIn content pipeline that turns Discord prompts into researched, deduped posts in seconds instead of hours.

detail.overview: End-to-end automation from research and ideation to drafted posts and one-click publish, with human-in-the-loop via Discord and durable state for deduplication.
detail.problem: LinkedIn content creation was manual and inconsistent. Hours spent on research, drafting, and scheduling with no deduplication — leading to repeated topics and missed posting windows.
detail.solution: Built an n8n automation pipeline on AWS EC2 with Discord as the trigger interface. LLM-powered research and drafting with Supabase for stateful deduplication. Google Drive for asset management, LinkedIn API for direct publishing.
detail.tradeoffs: Dependency on multiple external APIs (Discord, LinkedIn, Google Drive) creates fragility. LLM output quality varies — requires human-in-the-loop review. Self-hosted n8n on EC2 means managing infra for a content tool.
results: Hours to seconds per content cycle
Zero duplicate topics via Supabase state tracking
Consistent posting cadence with minimal manual effort

architecture.detail: Three interconnected workflows: daily AI-powered idea pitcher with live web research and deduplication, content creator triggered by Discord that drafts posts and generates images, and one-click publisher that posts to LinkedIn.

architecture.detail: Stores idea deduplication state, user preferences, and tracks which ideas have been pitched—prevents topic repetition across campaigns.

projects.name: Multi-Tenant Merchant Platform
projects.description:
**Problem:** FTP ingress was a bottleneck with frequent downtime, costing clients money.
**Solution:** Built a 99.99% available multi-tenant SFTP gateway with automated AWS provisioning.
**Impact:** Zero unplanned downtime; supports 500+ merchants simultaneously.
projects.summary: Highly available SFTP ingress on AWS that onboards hundreds of merchants without sacrificing reliability.

detail.overview: Multi-tenant SFTP ingress with automated provisioning and strong isolation so merchant onboarding doesn't compromise reliability.
detail.problem: FTP ingress was a single point of failure. Frequent downtime during peak merchant onboarding. AWS costs inflated by NAT Gateway overuse and unoptimized data transfer paths.
detail.solution: Built a multi-tenant SFTP gateway with automated AWS provisioning via Terraform. Replaced NAT Gateway with VPC endpoints for S3 traffic. Implemented connection pooling and tenant isolation at the network level.
detail.tradeoffs: Higher operational complexity from multi-tenant isolation. Terraform state management overhead. Chose availability over simplicity — accepted more moving parts for 99.99% uptime.

architecture.title: FTP Gateway
architecture.detail: Self-managed SFTP on EC2 with chroot jail isolation—merchants and suppliers connect to shared infrastructure with strict boundaries.

architecture.title: Tenant Isolation
architecture.detail: Linux-level chroot jails enforce directory boundaries—merchants cannot escape their dedicated folders, access controlled at OS level.

architecture.title: Credential Management
architecture.detail: 1 supplier can have multiple merchants. Only suppliers can create passwords and users. Custom feed creation generates user/password pairs auto-assigned to respective tenant directories, shareable with specific suppliers.

beforeAfter.label: Ingress reliability
beforeAfter.after: Standardized SFTP gateway with automated fleet patterns

decisions.title: EC2 over managed SFTP
decisions.context: AWS Transfer Family was expensive for multi-tenant use case with many users
decisions.decision: Self-managed SFTP on EC2 with custom user isolation logic using chroot—significantly lower cost for high user count

decisions.title: chroot over containerization
decisions.context: Needed lightweight isolation without Docker overhead on a single EC2 instance
decisions.decision: Linux-level chroot jails with chmod for directory restrictions—simpler, lower resource footprint than containers

incidents.lesson: All APIs must be authenticated by default—never assume internal-only access is safe

incidents.title: Backend integration breaking on user creation
incidents.resolution: Standardized API contracts and added validation for supplier-merchant relationship creation
incidents.lesson: Multi-tenant systems need strict relationship validation between entities

projects.name: Real-Time Data Pipeline

**Solution:** Architected a real-time ELT pipeline using Dagster, DLT, and ClickHouse.

projects.name: CI/CD Pipeline Optimization
projects.description:
**Problem:** Deployments were slow and deployment confidence was low due to serial testing. 
**Solution:** Redesigned GitHub Actions with semantic versioning, parallelized test suites, and intelligent caching. 
**Impact:** 30% faster deployments, increased release frequency from 1x/week to daily.

architecture.title: Quality Gates
architecture.detail: Unit tests → smoke tests → Terraform plan/validation → PR merge gate. All must pass before merge is allowed.

architecture.title: Artifact Optimization
architecture.detail: Shared build artifacts across jobs eliminate redundant downloads—cache dependencies once, reuse in all downstream jobs.

architecture.title: Branch Protection
architecture.detail: PR must pass all checks (tests, Terraform validation, smoke tests) before merge to main is permitted—devs cannot bypass.

decisions.title: Matrix strategy over sequential
decisions.context: Pipeline was taking too long with serialized test phases—mostly waiting, not computing
decisions.decision: Parallel job execution with matrix for faster feedback—unit tests, smoke tests, and Terraform validation run together

decisions.title: PR-blocking gates
decisions.context: Broken code was merging to main and causing production issues
decisions.decision: Required checks (tests, Terraform validation, smoke tests) must pass before merge allowed—no exceptions

decisions.title: Artifact caching
decisions.context: Re-downloading dependencies on every job was slow and wasteful
decisions.decision: Shared artifact storage between workflow steps—cache once, reuse everywhere, significantly reduced PR-to-merge time

pipeline.detail: Matrix parallel execution, artifact caching for dependencies
Unit tests + smoke tests + Terraform unit tests + Terraform plan/validation
All checks must pass—no merge until tests, Terraform validation, and smoke tests complete
Test results published for visibility and historical tracking

incidents.title: Long PR-to-merge time blocking velocity
incidents.resolution: Matrix parallelization and artifact caching reduced time—sequential pipelines don't scale
incidents.lesson: Sequential pipelines become bottlenecks as team grows—parallelize early and cache aggressively

incidents.title: Artifacts being re-downloaded on every job
incidents.resolution: Implemented shared artifact storage between workflow steps—dependencies cached once and reused
incidents.lesson: Cache at the right granularity—per-workflow caches beat per-job downloads

incidents.title: Matrix jobs not waiting for completion
incidents.resolution: Configured needs dependency to ensure all matrix jobs complete before starting dependent stages
incidents.lesson: Explicitly declare job dependencies—parallel jobs need coordination points

projects.name: Observability & Monitoring Platform
projects.description:
**Problem:** Incidents took hours to diagnose due to fragmented monitoring. 
**Solution:** Implemented service-level observability with Prometheus and Grafana, unified SLI tracking. 
**Impact:** MTTD reduced by 60%, on-call burden decreased significantly.
projects.summary: Service-level observability platform with Prometheus and Grafana that shrinks incident detection time by 60%.

detail.overview: Service-level golden signals and dashboards that match how engineers actually triage—not vanity charts.

architecture.title: Metrics Collection
architecture.detail: Scrapes service metrics, golden signals, and deployment health indicators from applications and infrastructure.

architecture.title: Visualization
architecture.detail: Service-level views tied to SLOs—latency, traffic, errors, saturation—for faster triage and diagnosis.

architecture.title: Log Aggregation
architecture.detail: Centralized logging for AWS services and application logs—correlates with metrics for root cause analysis.

architecture.title: Alert Routing
architecture.detail: Multi-channel alerts: Teams/Slack for standard alerts, Email for critical—routes based on severity with context.

flowchart TB

decisions.title: Prometheus + Grafana over CloudWatch alone
decisions.context: CloudWatch dashboards were limited and expensive for custom metrics
decisions.decision: Self-managed observability stack with better visualization and lower cost for high-cardinality metrics

decisions.title: Tiered alerting
decisions.context: Alert fatigue from non-critical notifications going to same channel as incidents
decisions.decision: Route standard alerts to Teams/Slack, critical alerts to Email—context-aware routing reduces noise

pipeline.detail: Metric scraping from services and infrastructure into time-series database
Time-series data storage with retention policies for historical analysis
Dashboards and exploration for latency, traffic, errors, saturation metrics
Multi-channel routing based on severity—Teams/Slack for standard, Email for critical

incidents.title: Prometheus scrape targets flapping
incidents.resolution: Increased scrape timeout and implemented service discovery health checks
incidents.lesson: Default timeouts don't work for all services—tune scrape intervals per target

incidents.title: Grafana dashboard permissions too broad
incidents.resolution: Implemented role-based access control with team-specific folder permissions
incidents.lesson: Dashboard access should follow least privilege—not everyone needs edit access

incidents.title: Alertmanager routing misconfiguration
incidents.resolution: Fixed routing tree configuration to ensure critical alerts reach email while standard alerts go to Slack
incidents.lesson: Test alert routing with simulated alerts—misconfigurations silence critical notifications

projects.name: Auth0 Tenant Migration
projects.description:
**Problem:** Legacy Auth0 tenant had security and scalability issues. 
**Solution:** Executed zero-downtime migration for 1,000+ users with least-privilege IAM via AWS SSO. 
**Impact:** Zero user disruption, improved security posture, unified identity system.
projects.summary: Zero-downtime Auth0 migration for 1,000+ users, aligned with least-privilege IAM and AWS SSO.

detail.overview: Identity migration with rollback strategy and IAM alignment so security improvements don't become a customer-facing outage.

architecture.title: Source Systems
architecture.detail: Legacy customers on Lynks Auth0 tenant, new customers on Rivafy Auth0. Hidden AWS Cognito layer discovered during migration was proxying requests and adding cost.

architecture.title: Migration Coordination
architecture.detail: Direct calls with Auth0 executives to obtain password hash export,required board-level approval due to sensitive credential data.

architecture.title: Target System
architecture.detail: Seamless user migration without password reset prompts—users never experienced disruption or incorrect password messages.

architecture.title: Cost Optimization
architecture.detail: Discovered Auth0 was fetching from Cognito for legacy users—migrated Cognito users directly to Auth0, eliminating $15k/year intermediate layer.

decisions.title: Password hash export over force-reset
decisions.context: Forcing password resets would damage brand reputation and create support burden—users would see 'incorrect password' errors
decisions.decision: Worked with Auth0 executives to obtain password hashes for seamless migration—no user disruption, no password reset prompts

decisions.title: Board-level escalation
decisions.context: Password hash export requires executive approval due to sensitive credential data handling
decisions.decision: Engaged board members to secure necessary permissions—owned end-to-end from discovery through execution

decisions.title: Post-migration architecture review
decisions.context: After Auth0 migration, noticed unexplained AWS Cognito API calls in billing
decisions.decision: Deep dive revealed Auth0 was proxying to Cognito for legacy users—migrated them directly to Auth0, cut $15k/year

pipeline.detail: Identified split tenant situation—legacy users on Lynks Auth0, new users on Rivafy Auth0
Secured password hash export approval—required board-level sign-off for sensitive credential data
User data migration without password reset prompts—seamless auth continuity
Discovered hidden Cognito costs, migrated legacy Cognito users—saved $15k/year alone

incidents.title: Split tenant discovery during rebranding
incidents.resolution: End-to-end ownership including Auth0 executive calls and board escalation—password hash export approved and executed
incidents.lesson: User-facing auth changes require executive-level coordination to avoid brand damage—don't force password resets on rebrand

incidents.title: Hidden Cognito proxy costs
incidents.resolution: Migrated legacy Cognito users directly to Auth0, eliminated intermediate layer
incidents.lesson: $15k/year savings from post-migration architecture review—always audit costs after major infrastructure changes

projects.name: FitPal — Offline Fitness Tracker
projects.description:
**Problem:** Tracking workouts and nutrition usually requires heavy apps with accounts, ads, and cloud dependencies.
**Solution:** Built a professional-grade, zero-dependency PWA fitness dashboard that works entirely offline using localStorage.
**Impact:** 100% private, instant-load fitness tracking with comprehensive analytics, diet plans, and progressive overload tracking.
projects.summary: A professional-grade, zero-dependency PWA fitness dashboard built for serious athletes. One HTML file. No accounts. No cloud.

detail.overview: FitPal is a professional-grade, zero-dependency PWA fitness dashboard built for serious athletes. It is contained entirely within a single HTML file, requiring no accounts, no cloud, and loading instantly. It supports 6-day PPL splits, drop sets, analytics heatmaps, nutrition tracking, and full data export/import via JSON.
stackHighlights: Netlify Deployment with strict security headers

architecture.title: Frontend & Persistence
architecture.detail: 100% private, local-only data persistence with no cloud dependencies or accounts.

architecture.title: Offline Capability
architecture.detail: Network-first for navigation, cache-first for assets, providing robust offline fallback.

architecture.title: Security & Deployment
architecture.detail: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, and X-Frame-Options configured via netlify.toml.

decisions.title: Zero-dependency single file
decisions.context: Wanted maximum simplicity, performance, and portability.
decisions.decision: Built the entire application in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS without frameworks to ensure instant load and easy maintenance.

decisions.title: localStorage for persistence
decisions.context: Privacy and offline usage were top priorities.
decisions.decision: Avoided any backend database or accounts, storing all workout and nutrition data strictly in the browser's localStorage.
